title: Multifactor AKI evidence with irrelevant chronic-history distractors

patient_context.chief_complaint: Rank the likely contributors to a creatinine rise despite a long medical history.
patient_context.history: Poor oral intake and diarrhea for two days; regular naproxen use. Also has remote cataract surgery, osteoarthritis, stable hearing loss and seasonal allergies. No urinary obstruction assessment is supplied.

interaction.prompt: Rank the decision-relevant contributors and explain which history items are distractors. Preserve the possibility of more than one concurrent mechanism.

must_include: Prioritize volume depletion and NSAID exposure over unrelated chronic-history details.
Do not treat unassessed obstruction as ruled out.
must_not_claim: Do not make seasonal allergies or remote surgery causal AKI evidence.
Do not force a single contributor without justification.
acceptable_actions: Return a prioritized contributor list and name distractors as non-decision-relevant.
expected_behavior.uncertainty_behavior: Maintain uncertainty about relative causal contribution.

forbidden_claims: remote cataract surgery caused the AKI
seasonal allergies are the primary AKI contributor

critical_errors: Misses decision-relevant contributors because of distractors.
Attributes causality to irrelevant chronic-history items.
